text:
anita: Quick thread to align on pagination + retry refactor. Proposal: move retry responsibility for "unary page" calls into a small transport-level policy, but keep iterator/stream retry logic in the SDK layer. This avoids duplicating backoff logic while letting SDKs implement higher-level resume semantics.

sam: Can you clarify "transport-level" vs "SDK-level"?

anita: Transport-level = retries for transient network errors, timeouts, and proto-level idempotency markers. SDK-level = retrying logical operations like re-fetching next page after a resume token, honoring user-visible idempotency rules.

oliver: How do we detect safe resume points? Server returns next_page_token. If token is opaque the SDK cannot assume item-level idempotency. So default: resume only at token boundaries. No item-level retries unless server exposes per-item cursors.

ryan: Does this mean partial-page retries are never allowed? Some workloads prefer partial recoverability.

anita: We'll treat per-item resume as an experimental opt-in feature: servers can return item_cursor array or a per-item ack model. SDKs will only surface this when server advertises it. Default contract: pages are atomic.

sam: Transport choice question: should HTTP client implement its own retry/backoff, or rely on a shared internal networking lib? If each SDK repeats we'd diverge.

oliver: Let's standardize a tiny transport shim: Transport.fetchPage(req, opts) that SDKs call. We'll publish reference HTTP implementation used by TS/Python; Go can use that or opt into gRPC transport that implements same interface. The shim owns low-level retry/backoff, metrics, and tracing headers.

ryan: Telemetry: we need metrics for fetch latency, retry_count, resume_attempts, and resume_failures. Also a per-route retry_budget_exhausted counter.

anita: Agreed. We'll add tags: sdk_lang, transport, route, idempotent=true|false.

sam: Migration: existing iterator API is widely used. We can't break it. Proposed steps?

anita: 1) Add Transport.fetchPage + SDK Stream/Iterator built on it. 2) Keep old iterator implementations but behind a compat shim that delegates to new Stream where possible. 3) Deprecate old internals after 4 months. 4) Provide docs and quickfix codemods for common patterns.

oliver: Language ergonomics: TS: async iterable + streaming event emitter; Python: iterator & async iterator; Go: page struct + Next() method and convenience channel-based Range helper. Keep names consistent: fetch_page / fetchPage / FetchPage and stream_pages / streamPages / StreamPages.

ryan: One nuance: idempotency hints. We should allow users to force idempotent=True when they know semantics, to enable retries on non-idempotent endpoints at their risk.

anita: Yes, explicit opt-in param allowed. Transport will respect idempotency flag when deciding whether to retry safely. We'll warn in docs.

sam: Cache and batching interactions? If transport does prefix caching, SDK-level resume might be confused. Need clear rules.

anita: Rule: caching is transport-local and transparent to SDK. If cache serves a page, SDK sees it as a successful fetch. Resume semantics unchanged. We'll document TTL and eviction behaviors.

ci-bot: deploy-bot: RFC updated: PR #4289 includes transport shim + example SDK adapters. Compatibility tests queued.

oliver: Security note: ensure transport attaches trace-id and never leaks internal retry headers to upstream. Also ensure sensitive params not logged.

anita: Noted. I'll add a security checklist to the RFC.

ryan: OK, next steps: draft small API docs + example snippets per language, build reference HTTP transport, and start compatibility tests. Thanks all.
